title: House leader confident Congress will pass 2027 budget on time, avert reenactment
summary: A leader of the House of Representatives expressed confidence that the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027 would be approved on time, ruling out the possibility of a reenacted budget.

blocks.text: A leader of the House of Representatives expressed confidence that the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027 would be approved on time, ruling out the possibility of a reenacted budget.
The House of Representatives approved the proposed 2027 national budget on third and final reading in October. The measure is now undergoing review in the Senate.

"That's the worst thing that can happen, reenactment. I believe we are on the right track in terms of pacing," House Committee on Appropriations vice chairperson Zia Alonto Adiong said in an online interview on Tuesday.
"The Senate is multitasking, doing the impeachment and the budget at the same time. There's nothing to worry about the budget being reenacted because they have set their timeline," he added.
Once the Senate approves its version of the budget, the differences between the House and Senate versions will be reconciled by the bicameral conference committee.
Congress is scheduled to go on Christmas recess on December 19, 2026, with sessions set to resume on January 17, 2027.

Adiong said any possible delay in the budget's approval would likely last only a few days, adding that lawmakers could adjust the session schedule to accommodate the ratification of the bicameral conference committee report.
"The most that we can actually expect as to the possible delay is only a few days. At puwede naman din po magkaroon ng adjustment doon sa session days para po sa ratification ng bicam," he said.
Meanwhile, Adiong said the House is working on establishing a transparency website that would allow the public to monitor government project funding and implementation.
The proposed platform was earlier announced by House Speaker Faustino Dy III.
"Ongoing po yung pagpu-put up nitong website na ito for each, for the succeeding years to come," Alonto Adiong said.

He added that the public would be able to access information on projects during the budget season, including their identification in each congressional district and their subsequent implementation. —LDF, GMA News
